summary.worker_summary_tail:
`greg doctor` now reports which of `claude`, `codex` and `aider` are installed, and the new test passes along with the two existing doctor tests (3 passed).

The report has a new `frontier_workers_installed` field, a map from each worker name to true or false. It is a read-only PATH lookup, so none of the workers are ever run.

It is informational only. It is not one of the readiness checks, so it cannot change `ready_for_linux_service` or the exit code.

The new test, in `tests/unit/test_greg_chromebook_doctor.py`, fakes the PATH lookup with only `codex` present. It asserts the field comes out as `{"claude": False, "codex": True, "aider": False}`. It also asserts the only subprocess call is the existing `systemctl --user show-environment` check, and that the new field is not among the readiness checks.

The code change is `frontier_workers()` plus the new field in `greg/doctor.py`.
